assumptions.statement: Testing and release procedures require validation against local law and authority before promotion to avoid legality omissions.
Alternate supply may introduce new contamination risks requiring explicit engineering validation before connection.

expected_effects.rationale: Modeling isolation explicitly clears the blockage in recovery review.
Explicit authority modeling improves visibility without claiming approval.

hypothesis: Water recovery can move from blocked to testable if source isolation, alternate supply, lab testing, and release authority are modeled explicitly using dependency order patterns.

queries: CIaC water public health warning interventions expected effects labor energy privacy public health governance accessibility scenario resilience

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Model delivered water fallback and conservative no-release default.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Alternate supply may introduce new contamination risk

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Require explicit dependency on external lab availability or internal kit validation.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Testing authority may be unavailable during disruption

acceptance_tests: No new survival-critical unmet demand is introduced.
No labor is shifted into untracked resident burden.
Privacy, consent, public-health, accessibility, and governance assumptions remain explicit.

title: Water Recovery Source Isolation and Alternate Supply Playbook
